input: Get a carbon monoxide detector for every floor

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing the number of floors determines exactly how many detectors to buy, and whether any special placement rules apply (e.g., basement, attic).
Whether this is a house, apartment, rental property, or office changes local code requirements, landlord permissions, and installation constraints.
Budget determines whether to go with basic plug-in units, battery-only models, or premium smart/interconnected detectors.
The user may want specific features like smart-home integration, combination smoke+CO units, or digital displays, which narrows the product choice.
Whether the home already has wired smoke detectors affects whether a hardwired combo unit is feasible or if battery/plug-in is the only option.
If the user wants to self-install vs. hire an electrician, the plan changes significantly in complexity, cost, and product type.
Knowing whether the goal is basic safety compliance, insurance/code requirement, or full smart-home alerting defines what 'done well' looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Buy and install CO detectors on every floor
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to purchase and set up a carbon monoxide detector on each floor of their home or building.

questions.title: How many floors need a detector?
questions.description: Find out the exact number of floors (including basement and attic if applicable) so the user knows precisely how many units to buy.

questions.title: Is this a house, apartment, or another building type?
questions.description: Identify the building type to surface any relevant local codes, landlord approval needs, or installation restrictions.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this purchase?
questions.description: Establish a budget range to filter detector options from basic (~$20/unit) to premium smart models (~$80+/unit).

questions.title: Do you want CO-only or combined smoke and CO units?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants dedicated CO detectors or combination smoke+CO devices, which affects product selection.

questions.title: Does your home have existing hardwired smoke detectors?
questions.description: Check the existing electrical setup to determine if hardwired interconnected units are a viable option or if battery/plug-in is the right fit.

questions.title: Will you install the detectors yourself or hire someone?
questions.description: Clarify who handles installation to tailor the plan toward a DIY walkthrough or locating a qualified electrician.

questions.title: What does success look like — safety, code compliance, or smart alerts?
questions.description: Understand the end goal so the recommended detectors match the right standard, whether that is basic safety, meeting a local code, or app-based monitoring.
